compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
Both review gates execute criterion work through runners whose return values cannot reliably distinguish clean execution from failed, cancelled, skipped, budget-shed, or resumed work. Plan-review failures can become empty successful checkpoints, while code review loses earlier successful work when a later criterion raises. A shared effective-policy snapshot alone cannot fix those execution facts.

## Approach
Add a narrow shared discovery kernel under `rebar.llm.review_kernel`. Define immutable `DiscoveryStagePlan` and `DiscoveryUnitPlan` inputs plus `DiscoveryStageResult` and typed per-unit outcomes: `success`, `resumed`, `skipped`, `shed`, `failed`, and `cancelled`. A plan carries stable unit ids, dependencies, prompt/contract/model/mode identities, context and policy digests, blocking capability, budget estimate, and gate-supplied execution callbacks.

The executor owns dependency-aware scheduling, explicit positive-budget shedding, usage accumulation, cancellation observation, and success-only checkpoint envelope creation. After RP-01 exhausts a local operation it preserves successful independent results and continues; a dependent of missing work becomes `skipped` with a dependency reason. Systemic configuration/provider initialization failures and cancellation abort remaining execution with exact completed-so-far accounting. Gate verdicts remain outside the executor.

Define a new versioned, digest-complete checkpoint/trace envelope. Its identity covers material, code/ref, effective-policy snapshot, prompt and contract, model/mode, topology, input context, dependencies, and namespace version. Only `success` and content-identical `resumed` units may be committed as reusable successes; failed, cancelled, skipped, and shed units remain missing. Legacy checkpoints are never read as new successes.

The typed trace is safe stored diagnostic data: normalized ids, outcomes, reason codes, usage, and lineage only. It excludes raw prompts, ticket/context bodies, provider responses, and secrets. No per-unit trace is added to review or review-status response contracts.

## Boundaries and Rationale
Keep policy selection, gate context construction, YAML/BPMN topology, provider-turn retry/output handling, checkpoint persistence, and final verdict decisions in their current owners. A focused execution kernel gives both gates the same trustworthy facts without building a second workflow interpreter or fighting RP-01 provider semantics.

## Testing
Use in-process contract tests with the real plan/result/envelope codecs and an injected stateful fake only at the model-call boundary. Tests assert exact call order, returned outcomes, usage, checkpoint eligibility, collateral state, and a clean retry after injected local failure. Negative controls prove a systemic failure aborts and a failed/shed/cancelled result never round-trips as success.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `DiscoveryStagePlan` and `DiscoveryStageResult` represent stable unit identity, dependencies, blocking capability, usage, and all six approved outcome kinds without gate-specific verdict fields.
- [ ] Given one exhausted local failure, the real executor retains earlier successes, executes later independent units, and marks dependent units skipped with the missing dependency id.
- [ ] Given a systemic initialization/configuration failure or cancellation, the executor stops remaining work and returns exact completed, failed, and cancelled accounting without fabricating usage or findings.
- [ ] A positive explicit budget deterministically sheds work that does not fit; omission is uncapped and zero is rejected by the contract rather than interpreted as disablement.
- [ ] The versioned envelope round-trips only digest-complete, content-identical success/resume records; injected failed, cancelled, skipped, shed, corrupt, and legacy envelopes remain missing.
- [ ] Stored trace serialization contains normalized outcome metadata and lineage but no raw prompt, ticket/context body, provider payload, or secret, and public review result schemas remain unchanged.
- [ ] Fault-injection tests prove restoration plus a clean rerun succeeds and that unrelated successful unit state is unchanged.
